//: Type checking only - noEmit is deliberate. build.mjs copies .mjs files
verbatim through the SPLICER preprocessor, and the browser loads them
natively as ES modules, so nothing here compiles anything.
checkJs is off by default: files opt in with a `// @ts-check` comment at
the top. That lets the codebase be typed a file at a time instead of
producing thousands of errors on day one.
A library tools/sync-vendor.mjs copies into chrome/player/modules (gitignored)
is typed by the declaration file beside it (hls.d.mts beside hls.mjs, which
TypeScript prefers to the script), the same whether the build has run or not.
It re-exports the npm package's own types; types/vendor-patches.d.ts adds what
FastStream's patches add and what the types lack (docs/notes/type-checking.md).
Without one, the check failed once the library was there: TypeScript read its
JavaScript and guessed types the code does not fit. typeChecked.test.mjs keeps
a declaration beside each imported one; the build ships none (tools/splicer.mjs).
